Article 3

Paragraph (1) Letter a Sufficiently Clear Letter b What is meant by exploitation is an action with or without the consent of the victim which includes prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical exploitation of sexual reproductive organs or unlawfully transferring/utilizing labor or transplanting organs and or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.

Letter c Sufficiently clear Letter d What is meant by witness is a person who sees, hears and experiences incidents of violence and human rights violations Letter e Mediation is conducted for cases of domestic violence that fall into the category of complaint offenses as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence.

Paragraph (2) Letter a What is meant by "physical violence" is an act that results in pain, illness, or serious injury such as slapping, hitting, spitting, pulling hair/grabbing, kicking, burning with hot objects, hitting/injuring with weapons, and/or resulting in disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Letter b What is meant by "psychological violence" is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. Psychological violence can take the form of emotional abuse such as insults, hurtful comments or degrading self-esteem, isolating the wife from the outside world, threatening or frightening as a means of imposing one's will.

Letter c What is meant by "sexual violence" is any act that violates a person's human dignity based on gender discrimination that targets a person's body and sexuality, which results in or may result in physical, psychological, economic, sexual, political and/or social harm or suffering to the victim. This formulation is the essence of the findings of 15 forms of sexual violence, including: 1) Rape; An attack in the form of forced sexual intercourse using the penis towards the victim's vagina, anus or mouth. It can also use fingers or other objects. The attack is carried out with violence, threats of violence, detention, psychological pressure, abuse of power, or by taking advantage of a coercive environment. Indecent assault is another term for rape known in the Indonesian legal system. This term is used when rape is committed outside of forced penetration of the penis into the vagina and when sexual intercourse occurs with a person who is not yet able to give full consent, for example against a child or someone under 18 years of age.

Sexual violence also includes isolating (distancing) the wife from her spiritual needs, forcing sexual intercourse, imposing one's own sexual preferences or not paying attention to the wife's satisfaction. Sexual violence can also take the form of forced sexual intercourse committed against a person residing within the household, forced sexual intercourse against one person within the household with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Letter d What is meant by "economic neglect" is neglecting the economic needs of the wife or children or family members or relatives such as not providing for the wife, even spending the wife's money, not providing or withholding the wages of domestic workers or drivers and includes acts of restricting and/or prohibiting family members from working appropriately.

Letter e What is meant by "restriction of movement" is restricting the movement of the wife or children in developing their potential both for economic and social purposes such as prohibiting them from gathering and socializing in the community and restricting the movement of relatives such as preventing domestic workers or drivers from communicating or having contact with their families.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Sigi Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sigi.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the people's representative institution of the Sigi Regency Region as an element of the Regional government administration.
5. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Work Unit of Sigi Regency.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including a child in the womb.
7. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
9. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of acts of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.
10. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death.
12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
14. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence. 15. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of violations of Human Rights (HAM), or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals.
16. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
18. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
19. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of acts of violence to their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
20. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.
21. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
22. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organization (NGO) that provides assistance.
23. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychosocial and legal services.
24. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services in the context of empowerment of women and children victims of acts of violence.
25. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in the context of implementing prevention and protection activities for women and children victims of acts of violence.
26. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
27. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF SIGI REGENCY

NUMBER 9 YEAR 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and state. Therefore the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obliged to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of continuous work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, among others the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore the Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is born to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling for victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academic Parties, Journalist Parties and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

Article 20

1. The Regional Government is obliged to supervise the implementation of protection of women and children from acts of violence. (2) Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), is carried out professionally based on the principles of transparency, accountability and participation.

Article 11

Prevention actions for acts of violence against women and children implemented by the community may be in the form of:
a. actively participating in programs and activities initiated by the Government, Regional Government, or other parties as long as they do not conflict with the principles of protection for women and children established in this Regional Regulation;
b. activities initiated by the community as long as they do not conflict with the principles of protection for women and children established in this Regional Regulation.

Article 21

The community may supervise the implementation of protection of women and children from victims of violence, which is organized by the Regional Government directly or indirectly.

CHAPTER IV

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 6

Obligations and responsibilities in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence are the joint responsibility of:
a. Regional Government;
b. community.

Article 23

1. The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations and non-governmental organizations that implement protection of women and children from discrimination and acts of violence.
2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), is in accordance with the financial capacity of the Region, and is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of Regional finance.

Article 8

The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 6 letter b, include prevention, handling and recovery actions towards women and children victims of acts of violence.

Article 13

Paragraph (1) Letter a What is meant by complaint services is a series of actions taken by the organizers of integrated service institutions to follow up on direct reports from victims of violence against women and children, families and/or the community.

Letter b What is meant by health services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative aspects.

Letter c Sufficiently Clear Letter d What is meant by repatriation is facilitation provided by the Regional Government to victims who request to be returned to their region of origin.

Letter e Sufficiently Clear Letter f What is meant by social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.

Paragraph (2) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (3) Sufficiently clear

Article 15

1. Customary institutions that provide services for resolving cases of violence against women and children victims of acts of violence may carry out their functions in accordance with applicable customary provisions as long as they do not conflict with the principles and objectives established in this Regional Regulation.
2. Certain cases that have consequences for criminal acts based on positive law related to the service function of customary institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) are transferred to the competent authority.
3. Decisions and sanctions regarding cases of violence against women and children other than the provisions regulated in paragraph (2) that are produced through customary courts may be implemented in accordance with local customary provisions.

Article 19

Paragraph (1) What is meant by guidance on the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of violence is an effort made by the Regional Government and the community to realize the achievement of the objectives of prevention and protection of women and children victims of violence What is meant by supervision of the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of violence is a process of activities aimed at ensuring that efforts made by the Regional Government and the community run efficiently and effectively in accordance with plans and provisions of laws and regulations.

Paragraph (2) Sufficiently Clear Paragraph (3) Sufficiently Clear

Article 4

Letter a What is meant by the right to have one's dignity respected is upholding human rights Letter b What is meant by the right to complaint handling is the availability of a special integrated service unit by officers Letter c What is meant by the right to determine one's own decision is the victim's right to choose service actions, the process to be undertaken, and the parties involved in handling the case.

Letter d What is meant by the right to information is the right to obtain information, statements, ideas, and signs containing value, meaning, and messages, whether data, facts or explanations that can be seen, heard, and read presented in various packages and formats in accordance with the development of information and communication technology both electronically and non-electronically related to acts of violence.

Letter e Sufficiently clear Letter f What is meant by the right to compensation includes economic empowerment, repatriation costs, health insurance, and education or skills.

Letter g Sufficiently Clear Letter h What is meant by the right to assistance includes psychologists, psychiatrists, health experts, clergy, advocates, and family members. An assistant is an individual who works as a volunteer to provide protection and support to women and children victims of violence during the judicial process, these assistants can come from family members, friends or independent organizations that provide attention to witnesses and victims or advocates.

Letter i What is meant by the victim's right to rehabilitation includes: access to medical services for physical and psychological recovery, legal assistance to restore civil rights

Letter c What is meant by "sexual violence" is any act that violates a person's human dignity based on gender discrimination that targets a person's body and sexuality, which results in or may result in physical, psychological, economic, sexual, political and/or social harm or suffering to the victim. This formulation is the essence of the findings of 15 forms of sexual violence, including: 1) Rape; An attack in the form of forced sexual intercourse using the penis towards the victim's vagina, anus or mouth. It can also use fingers or other objects. The attack is carried out with violence, threats of violence, detention, psychological pressure, abuse of power, or by taking advantage of a coercive environment. Indecent assault is another term for rape known in the Indonesian legal system. This term is used when rape is committed outside of forced penetration of the penis into the vagina and when sexual intercourse occurs with a person who is not yet able to give full consent, for example against a child or someone under 18 years of age.

Sexual violence also includes isolating (distancing) the wife from her spiritual needs, forcing sexual intercourse, imposing one's own sexual preferences or not paying attention to the wife's satisfaction. Sexual violence can also take the form of forced sexual intercourse committed against a person residing within the household, forced sexual intercourse against one person within the household with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Letter d What is meant by "economic neglect" is neglecting the economic needs of the wife or children or family members or relatives such as not providing for the wife, even spending the wife's money, not providing or withholding the wages of domestic workers or drivers and includes acts of restricting and/or prohibiting family members from working appropriately.

Letter e What is meant by "restriction of movement" is restricting the movement of the wife or children in developing their potential both for economic and social purposes such as prohibiting them from gathering and socializing in the community and restricting the movement of relatives such as preventing domestic workers or drivers from communicating or having contact with their families.

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and state. Therefore the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obliged to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of continuous work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, among others the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore the Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is born to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling for victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academic Parties, Journalist Parties and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF SIGI REGENCY

NUMBER 9 YEAR 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and state. Therefore the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obliged to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of continuous work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, among others the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore the Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is born to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling for victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academic Parties, Journalist Parties and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF SIGI REGENCY

NUMBER 9 YEAR 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and state. Therefore the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obliged to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of continuous work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, among others the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore the Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is born to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling for victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academic Parties, Journalist Parties and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

NUMBER 9 YEAR 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and state. Therefore the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obliged to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of continuous work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, among others the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore the Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is born to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling for victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academic Parties, Journalist Parties and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

b. activities initiated by the community as long as they do not conflict with the principles of protection for women and children established in this Regional Regulation.

Article 21

The community may supervise the implementation of protection of women and children from victims of violence, which is organized by the Regional Government directly or indirectly.

Article 15

1. Customary institutions that provide services for resolving cases of violence against women and children victims of acts of violence may carry out their functions in accordance with applicable customary provisions as long as they do not conflict with the principles and objectives established in this Regional Regulation.

11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death.
12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
14. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence. 15. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of violations of Human Rights (HAM), or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals.

17. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.

19. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of acts of violence to their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
20. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.
21. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.

CHAPTER V

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 9

1. In implementing protection for women and children victims of violence, the community may: a. form family partners at the kelurahan/village level by the community;
b. form women and children protection units within community organizations;
c. conduct socialization of women's and children's rights independently; d. provide first aid to victims; and e. report to the competent authority if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

CHAPTER IV

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 6

Obligations and responsibilities in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence are the joint responsibility of:
a. Regional Government;
b. community.

Article 20

1. The Regional Government is obliged to supervise the implementation of protection of women and children from acts of violence. (2) Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), is carried out professionally based on the principles of transparency, accountability and participation.

CHAPTER VIII

THE ROLE OF CUSTOMARY INSTITUTIONS IN THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF ACTS OF VIOLENCE

Article 21

The community may supervise the implementation of protection of women and children from victims of violence, which is organized by the Regional Government directly or indirectly.

Article 23

1. The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations and non-governmental organizations that implement protection of women and children from discrimination and acts of violence.
2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), is in accordance with the financial capacity of the Region, and is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of Regional finance.

Article 14

1. In order to maximize the role of the Regional Government in implementing the service function for women and children victims of acts of violence, a safe house is established.
2. Further provisions regarding safe house services as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

REGENT OF SIGI

HAS DECIDED:

To Establish: REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE.

Article 15

1. Customary institutions that provide services for resolving cases of violence against women and children victims of acts of violence may carry out their functions in accordance with applicable customary provisions as long as they do not conflict with the principles and objectives established in this Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and state. Therefore the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obliged to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of continuous work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, among others the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore the Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is born to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling for victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academic Parties, Journalist Parties and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF SIGI REGENCY

NUMBER 9 YEAR 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and state. Therefore the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obliged to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of continuous work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, among others the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore the Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is born to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling for victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academic Parties, Journalist Parties and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of violations of Human Rights (HAM), or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and state. Therefore the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obliged to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of continuous work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, among others the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore the Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is born to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling for victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academic Parties, Journalist Parties and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

Article 23

2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), is in accordance with the financial capacity of the Region, and is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of Regional finance.

Article 21

The community may supervise the implementation of protection of women and children from victims of violence, which is organized by the Regional Government directly or indirectly.

Letter c What is meant by "sexual violence" is any act that violates a person's human dignity based on gender discrimination that targets a person's body and sexuality, which results in or may result in physical, psychological, economic, sexual, political and/or social harm or suffering to the victim. It can also use fingers or other objects. The attack is carried out with violence, threats of violence, detention, psychological pressure, abuse of power, or by taking advantage of a coercive environment. Indecent assault is another term for rape known in the Indonesian legal system. This term is used when rape is committed outside of forced penetration of the penis into the vagina and when sexual intercourse occurs with a person who is not yet able to give full consent, for example against a child or someone under 18 years of age.

Sexual violence also includes isolating (distancing) the wife from her spiritual needs, forcing sexual intercourse, imposing one's own sexual preferences or not paying attention to the wife's satisfaction. Based on the provisions in Article 41 of Law Number 1 of 1974 concerning Marriage ("Marriage Law") it is stated that the consequences of the dissolution of a marriage due to divorce are:
a. Both mother or father remain obligated to care for and educate their children, solely based on the interests of the child, if there is a dispute regarding custody of the children, the Court gives its decision. b. The father is responsible for all maintenance and education costs required by the child, if the father in reality cannot fulfill such obligations the court may determine that the mother shares in bearing such costs. c. The Court may require the former husband to provide living expenses and/or determine an obligation for the former wife.

The only rule that clearly and explicitly provides guidance for judges in deciding the granting of custody rights over the child is contained in Article 105 of the Compilation of Islamic Law (KHI) which states: "In the event of divorce:
a. custody of a child who is not yet mumayyiz or not yet 12 years old is the mother's right. b. custody of a child who is already mumayyiz is handed over to the child to choose between the father or mother as the holder of custody rights. c. maintenance costs are borne by the father."

ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF SIGI REGENCY

NUMBER 9 YEAR 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and state. Therefore the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obliged to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of continuous work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, among others the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore the Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is born to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling for victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academic Parties, Journalist Parties and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

Letter b What is meant by the principle of justice, is a mental state of every human being who naturally/innately wants to obtain a sense of justice as part of society and/or fulfilled sense of justice for every person in their position as citizens. In relation to the protection of women and children victims of acts of violence whose implementation is regulated through this regional regulation, must fulfill the principle of justice at least including gender equality, legal certainty, presumption of innocence, equal rights before the law, not blaming the victim, best interests for the victim. The meaning of best interests for the victim, that in the process of handling cases experienced by victims, all parties involved in it, both government, society, legislative, executive, judicial bodies must place the interests of victims as the most important in all situations.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and state. Therefore the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obliged to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of continuous work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, among others the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore the Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is born to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling for victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academic Parties, Journalist Parties and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

Letter c What is meant by "sexual violence" is any act that violates a person's human dignity based on gender discrimination that targets a person's body and sexuality, which results in or may result in physical, psychological, economic, sexual, political and/or social harm or suffering to the victim. This formulation is the essence of the findings of 15 forms of sexual violence, including: 1) Rape; An attack in the form of forced sexual intercourse using the penis towards the victim's vagina, anus or mouth. It can also use fingers or other objects. The attack is carried out with violence, threats of violence, detention, psychological pressure, abuse of power, or by taking advantage of a coercive environment. Indecent assault is another term for rape known in the Indonesian legal system. This term is used when rape is committed outside of forced penetration of the penis into the vagina and when sexual intercourse occurs with a person who is not yet able to give full consent, for example against a child or someone under 18 years of age.

Sexual violence also includes isolating (distancing) the wife from her spiritual needs, forcing sexual intercourse, imposing one's own sexual preferences or not paying attention to the wife's satisfaction. Sexual violence can also take the form of forced sexual intercourse committed against a person residing within the household, forced sexual intercourse against one person within the household with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Letter d What is meant by "economic neglect" is neglecting the economic needs of the wife or children or family members or relatives such as not providing for the wife, even spending the wife's money, not providing or withholding the wages of domestic workers or drivers and includes acts of restricting and/or prohibiting family members from working appropriately.

Letter e What is meant by "restriction of movement" is restricting the movement of the wife or children in developing their potential both for economic and social purposes such as prohibiting them from gathering and socializing in the community and restricting the movement of relatives such as preventing domestic workers or drivers from communicating or having contact with their families.

ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF SIGI REGENCY

NUMBER 9 YEAR 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and state. Therefore the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obliged to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of continuous work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, among others the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore the Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is born to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling for victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academic Parties, Journalist Parties and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Sigi Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sigi.

11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death.

13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of violations of Human Rights (HAM), or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals.

25. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in the context of implementing prevention and protection activities for women and children victims of acts of violence.
26. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
27. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death.
12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
14. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence. 15. Therefore the Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is born to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF SIGI REGENCY

NUMBER 9 YEAR 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and state. Therefore the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obliged to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of continuous work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, among others the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore the Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is born to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling for victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academic Parties, Journalist Parties and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and state. Therefore the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obliged to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of continuous work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, among others the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore the Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is born to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling for victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academic Parties, Journalist Parties and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and state. Therefore the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obliged to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of continuous work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, among others the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore the Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is born to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling for victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academic Parties, Journalist Parties and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
14. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence. 15. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of violations of Human Rights (HAM), or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals.

20. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF SIGI REGENCY

NUMBER 9 YEAR 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and state. Therefore the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obliged to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of continuous work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, among others the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore the Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is born to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling for victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academic Parties, Journalist Parties and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Sigi Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sigi.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the people's representative institution of the Sigi Regency Region as an element of the Regional government administration.
5. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Work Unit of Sigi Regency.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including a child in the womb.
7. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
9. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of acts of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.
10. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death.
12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
14. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence. 15. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of violations of Human Rights (HAM), or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals.
16. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
18. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
19. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of acts of violence to their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
20. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.
21. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
22. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organization (NGO) that provides assistance.
23. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychosocial and legal services.
24. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services in the context of empowerment of women and children victims of acts of violence.
25. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in the context of implementing prevention and protection activities for women and children victims of acts of violence.
26. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
27. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Letter c What is meant by "sexual violence" is any act that violates a person's human dignity based on gender discrimination that targets a person's body and sexuality, which results in or may result in physical, psychological, economic, sexual, political and/or social harm or suffering to the victim. This formulation is the essence of the findings of 15 forms of sexual violence, including: 1) Rape; An attack in the form of forced sexual intercourse using the penis towards the victim's vagina, anus or mouth. It can also use fingers or other objects. The attack is carried out with violence, threats of violence, detention, psychological pressure, abuse of power, or by taking advantage of a coercive environment. Indecent assault is another term for rape known in the Indonesian legal system. This term is used when rape is committed outside of forced penetration of the penis into the vagina and when sexual intercourse occurs with a person who is not yet able to give full consent, for example against a child or someone under 18 years of age.

Sexual violence also includes isolating (distancing) the wife from her spiritual needs, forcing sexual intercourse, imposing one's own sexual preferences or not paying attention to the wife's satisfaction. Sexual violence can also take the form of forced sexual intercourse committed against a person residing within the household, forced sexual intercourse against one person within the household with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
